summary: The agent implemented the requested map-entry collection mappings and passed all 3,641 baseline tests plus 30 of 32 new tests, but it incorrectly relaxed method validation for Map-to-Stream and Stream-to-Map methods. The two hidden boundary cases therefore compiled when they should have been rejected.
quick_failure_summary: Map-to-Stream and Stream-to-Map declarations are accepted even though the feature is limited to iterable or array mappings.

details.reasoning: The agent completed a substantial, mostly correct implementation, but its MethodRetrievalProcessor exceptions are too broad: any Map source is exempted when the result is a Java-standard-library iterable-or-stream type, and any Map result is exempted when the source is an iterable-or-stream type. This permits Map-to-Stream and Stream-to-Map declarations even though only iterable and array directions were requested. The hidden boundary test failed for both compiler variants because compilation succeeded instead of producing the existing iterable/non-iterable diagnostics.
details.secondary_factors: The agent added positive feature tests and ran focused and neighboring suites, but did not add a negative test preserving the repository's distinct stream mapping family boundary.

justification.issue_description: The implementation fails to preserve the boundary between the new Map/Iterable entry mappings and the separately modeled Stream mapping family.
justification.evidence: The prompt repeatedly limits the feature to an 'iterable or array result' and an 'iterable or array source element'; it never includes Stream. The visible codebase separately defines SourceMethod.isIterableMapping() and SourceMethod.isStreamMapping(), and MethodRetrievalProcessor uses isStreamTypeOrIterableFromJavaStdLib() to enforce family boundaries. Existing ErroneousStreamMappingTest coverage also expects Stream-to-non-iterable and non-iterable-to-Stream declarations to fail. The agent changed validation to test only !resultType.isMapType() and !parameterType.isMapType(), rather than exempting only the precise iterable-to-map and map-to-iterable cases.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than an undocumented hidden-test expectation: the iterable/array scope is explicit in the prompt and the Stream distinction is reinforced by visible production code and existing tests. A competent implementation should have narrowed the validation exceptions to parameterType.isIterableType() with resultType.isMapType(), and parameterType.isMapType() with resultType.isIterableType().

problem_assessment.notes: The task is broad and requires coordinated compiler-model, template, type-selection, constructor, qualifier, wildcard, and inheritance changes. The failed boundary requirement is nevertheless clear: the description expressly names iterable and array containers, while the repository models Stream separately. The reference solution demonstrates the task is solvable, and the new tests deterministically exercise the stated behavior.

evidence: The verifier completed normally: baseline grading reported 3,641/3,641 passing and new-test grading reported 30/32 passing.
Both new-test failures are assertion failures stating that compilation succeeded when failure was expected; they directly exercise the agent's broadened MethodRetrievalProcessor conditions.

The trace encountered a missing rg executable and a GitHub API rate limit, but the agent immediately used find/grep alternatives, successfully cloned upstream separately, completed the implementation, and ran multiple Maven validations.
No repeated bootstrap, dependency, permission, runtime, or shared-helper failure diverted validation or prevented the changed code from being exercised.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the two failures are explained by an over-broad validation exemption in the implementation.
